title: 自序
label: 自序 (呐喊)
credit: Text: 自序, Lu Xun's (鲁迅) preface to 呐喊 (1923; dated 3 December 1922), from Chinese Wikisource (zh.wikisource.org/wiki/吶喊, section 自序, revision 11120768), public domain. Glosses, notes and translation added by Claude.

chapters.text: 我在年青时候也曾经做过许多梦，后来大半忘却了，但自己也并不以为可惜。
chapters.translation: When I was young I too had a great many dreams. Most of them I later forgot, and I do not think that a pity.
chapters.note: This is Lu Xun's preface to 呐喊, his first book of stories. 年青 "young" is today usually written 年轻. 做梦 "have a dream" is split here: 做过许多梦 "have had many dreams". 忘却 is the bookish 忘记 "forget". 并不 "not at all": 并 stresses the 不.

chapters.text: 所谓回忆者，虽说可以使人欢欣，有时也不免使人寂寞，使精神的丝缕还牵着已逝的寂寞的时光，又有什么意味呢，而我偏苦于不能全忘却，这不能全忘的一部分，到现在便成了呐喊的来由。
chapters.translation: As for what is called remembering: though it can make a person glad, at times it cannot help making him lonely too. What is the point of letting the threads of the mind still tug at lonely times that are already gone? Yet my trouble is that I cannot forget them completely, and the part I cannot forget has now become the reason for 呐喊.
chapters.note: 所谓…者 "what is called …": 者 after a noun closes off the topic, as in classical Chinese. 苦于 "suffer from": 苦于不能全忘却 "suffer from not being able to forget completely". 呐喊 is the book's title: a shout, a battle cry. In English it is usually called Call to Arms.

chapters.text: 我有四年多，曾经常常，——几乎是每天，出入于质铺和药店里，年纪可是忘却了，总之是药店的柜台正和我一样高，质铺的是比我高一倍，我从一倍高的柜台外送上衣服或首饰去，在侮蔑里接了钱，再到一样高的柜台上给我久病的父亲去买药。
chapters.translation: For more than four years I went often (almost every day, in fact) in and out of a pawnshop and a medicine shop. How old I was I have forgotten; anyway, the counter of the medicine shop was just my height, and the pawnshop's was twice my height. Over the counter twice my height I handed up clothes or jewellery, took the money amid contempt, and then went to the counter of my own height to buy medicine for my father, who had long been ill.
chapters.note: 出入于质铺 "go in and out at a pawnshop": 于 after a verb is "at, in". 比我高一倍 "higher than me by one times": twice as high. 送上…去 "hand up (to there)". Lu Xun's father died in 1896, when Lu Xun was fifteen.

chapters.text: 回家之后，又须忙别的事了，因为开方的医生是最有名的，以此所用的药引也奇特：冬天的芦根，经霜三年的甘蔗，蟋蟀要原对的，结子的平地木，……多不是容易办到的东西。
chapters.translation: Back home I had other things to rush about, because the doctor who wrote the prescriptions was the most famous one, and so the "guides" he used with his medicines were out of the ordinary too: reed roots dug in winter, sugar cane that had been through three years of frost, crickets that had to be an original pair, ardisia that had set its seed… mostly things not easy to get hold of.
chapters.note: 药引 is a term of Chinese medicine: an extra ingredient said to lead the drugs to where they should work. It is not in CC-CEDICT. 蟋蟀要原对的 "the crickets had to be original-pair ones": a male and a female caught together. 以此 "because of this": 以 "by" + 此 "this", a classical pair. 所用的 "what (he) used": 所 before a verb makes "what is …-ed".

chapters.text: 然而我的父亲终于日重一日的亡故了。
wfw: -ly: often Lu Xun's spelling of 地 before a verb
chapters.translation: And yet my father grew worse day by day, and died in the end.
chapters.note: 日重一日 "a day heavier than the day before": getting worse each day. 的 here does the work of today's 地: it makes the phrase before it an adverb.

chapters.text: 有谁从小康人家而坠入困顿的么，我以为在这途路中，大概可以看见世人的真面目；我要到Ｎ进Ｋ学堂去了，仿佛是想走异路，逃异地，去寻求别样的人们。
chapters.translation: Has anyone fallen from a comfortable family into hardship? On that road, I think, one can probably see what people are really like. I was going to N to enter the K Academy, as if I wanted to take a different road, flee to a different place, and look for a different kind of people.
chapters.note: 小康 "comfortably off": a family with enough. 么 is the old spelling of the question particle 吗. N is Nanjing, and the K Academy is the Jiangnan Naval Academy (江南水师学堂), which Lu Xun entered in 1898. Like the S of 一件小事, the letters are his.

chapters.text: 我的母亲没有法，办了八元的川资，说是由我的自便；然而伊哭了，这正是情理中的事，因为那时读书应试是正路，所谓学洋务，社会上便以为是一种走投无路的人，只得将灵魂卖给鬼子，要加倍的奚落而且排斥的，而况伊又看不见自己的儿子了。
wfw: at the end of one's road
-ly: often Lu Xun's spelling of 地 before a verb
chapters.translation: My mother had no other way. She got together eight dollars for the journey and said I could do as I pleased. But she wept, which was only natural, because in those days the proper road was to study the classics and sit the examinations. Anyone who studied so-called foreign affairs was taken by society for a man at the end of his road, who had no choice but to sell his soul to the foreign devils, and he was jeered at and shut out twice over. And what was more, she would no longer see her son.
chapters.note: 伊 is "she": Lu Xun wrote 伊 for a woman, before 她 caught on. 元 is the silver dollar. 读书应试 "read the books and sit the exams": the old road to office through the civil-service examinations. 洋务 "foreign affairs": Western learning and the new schools. 鬼子 "devils" is a hostile word for foreigners. 而况 is the bookish 何况 "what is more"; it is not in CC-CEDICT.

chapters.text: 然而我也顾不得这些事，终于到Ｎ去进了Ｋ学堂了，在这学堂里，我才知道世上还有所谓格致、算学、地理、历史、绘图和体操。
wfw: cannot stop for, have no time to mind
chapters.translation: But I could not stop for any of that. In the end I went to N and entered the K Academy, and in that academy I learned for the first time that the world held such things as natural science, mathematics, geography, history, drawing and gymnastics.
chapters.note: 格致 is the late-Qing word for Western natural science, short for 格物致知 "examine things to extend knowledge", from the classic 大学. 算学 is the old word for mathematics (today 数学); it is not in CC-CEDICT. 才 "only then": he had never heard of them before.

chapters.text: 生理学并不教，但我们却看到些木版的全体新论和化学卫生论之类了。
wfw: A New Treatise on the Body (a book of anatomy, 1851)
The Chemistry of Common Life (a translated book)
chapters.translation: Physiology was not taught, but we did get to see woodblock editions of books such as A New Treatise on the Body and The Chemistry of Common Life.
chapters.note: 全体新论 (1851) was a book of Western anatomy in Chinese by the missionary doctor Benjamin Hobson. 化学卫生论 was a Chinese version of J. F. W. Johnston's The Chemistry of Common Life. The book prints the titles without any marks around them.

chapters.text: 我还记得先前的医生的议论和方药，和现在所知道的比较起来，便渐渐的悟得中医不过是一种有意的或无意的骗子，同时又很起了对于被骗的病人和他的家族的同情；而且从译出的历史上，又知道了日本维新是大半发端于西方医学的事实。
wfw: -ly: often Lu Xun's spelling of 地 before a verb
chapters.translation: I still remembered the talk and the prescriptions of the doctors from before, and when I set them beside what I now knew, I came little by little to see that Chinese doctors were nothing but cheats, knowing or unknowing. At the same time a deep sympathy arose in me for the sick who had been cheated, and for their families. And from the translated histories I also learned that Japan's reform had begun, for the most part, with Western medicine.
chapters.note: 和…比较起来 "compared with …". 悟得 "came to realise": 得 after a verb is "get, reach". 很起了…的同情 "a great sympathy … arose": 起 "rise". 维新 "reform" is here the Meiji Restoration of 1868. 发端于 "have its start in".

chapters.text: 因为这些幼稚的知识，后来便使我的学籍列在日本一个乡间的医学专门学校里了。
chapters.translation: Because of this childish knowledge, my name was later entered on the books of a medical college in the Japanese countryside.
chapters.note: The college was the Sendai Medical School (仙台医学专门学校), which Lu Xun entered in 1904. 学籍 is a student's registration: his name on the school's roll.

chapters.text: 我的梦很美满，预备卒业回来，救治像我父亲似的被误的病人的疾苦，战争时候便去当军医，一面又促进了国人对于维新的信仰。
wfw: like, as if (after what it compares)
chapters.translation: My dream was a happy one. When I graduated I would come home and cure the suffering of the sick who, like my father, had been harmed by bad treatment; in time of war I would serve as an army doctor; and at the same time I would strengthen my countrymen's faith in reform.
chapters.note: 卒业 is the old word for "graduate", still the Japanese one (today 毕业). 像…似的 "like …": 像我父亲似的 "like my father". 被误 "harmed by mistakes": 误 is "mislead, harm".

chapters.text: 我已不知道教授微生物学的方法，现在又有了怎样的进步了，总之那时是用了电影，来显示微生物的形状的，因此有时讲义的一段落已完，而时间还没有到，教师便映些风景或时事的画片给学生看，以用去这多馀的光阴。
chapters.translation: I no longer know what progress has been made since then in the way microbiology is taught, but at that time projected pictures were used to show the shapes of microbes. So sometimes, when a section of the lecture was finished and the time was not yet up, the teacher would show the students pictures of scenery or of the news, to use up the time left over.
chapters.note: 电影 today is "film", but what was shown here were lantern slides, still pictures thrown on a screen. 多馀 is the 1923 spelling of 多余 "spare, left over": 馀 is the old form of 余 in this sense, and it is kept as printed. 以 before a verb is "so as to".

chapters.text: 其时正当日、俄战争的时候，关于战事的画片自然也就比较的多了，我在这一个讲堂中，便须常常随喜我那同学们的拍手和喝采。
wfw: -ly: often Lu Xun's spelling of 地 before a verb
chapters.translation: It was just the time of the Russo-Japanese War, so naturally there were rather a lot of pictures of the fighting, and in that lecture hall I often had to join in my classmates' clapping and cheering.
chapters.note: The Russo-Japanese War of 1904 and 1905 was fought in Manchuria, on Chinese soil. 随喜 is a Buddhist word, "rejoice along with (another's good deed)": here, bitterly, "join in". 喝采 is the 1923 spelling of 喝彩 "cheer"; CC-CEDICT has both, and it is kept as printed.

chapters.text: 有一回，我竟在画片上忽然会见我久违的许多中国人了，一个绑在中间，许多站在左右，一样是强壮的体格，而显出麻木的神情。
chapters.translation: Once, in a picture, I suddenly met a great many Chinese, whom I had not seen for a long time. One was tied up in the middle and many stood around him. All of them were strongly built, and yet they wore a look of numbness.
chapters.note: 竟 "to my surprise". 会见 "meet" is the formal word for meeting a visitor, and 久违 "long unseen" is the greeting for an old friend; Lu Xun uses both of faces in a picture.

chapters.text: 据解说，则绑着的是替俄国做了军事上的侦探，正要被日军砍下头颅来示众，而围着的便是来赏鉴这示众的盛举的人们。
chapters.translation: According to the commentary, the one tied up had spied for Russia in military matters, and was about to have his head cut off by the Japanese army as a public example; and the ones around him were people who had come to enjoy the grand spectacle of that example.
chapters.note: 示众 "show to the crowd": a punishment done in public, to be seen. 赏鉴 "appreciate", as one would a work of art: Lu Xun's irony. 则 "then": 据解说，则… "by the commentary, (it was that) …". 绑着的 "the one tied up": 的 with no noun after it.

chapters.text: 这一学年没有完毕，我已经到了东京了，因为从那一回以后，我便觉得医学并非一件紧要事，凡是愚弱的国民，即使体格如何健全，如何茁壮，也只能做毫无意义的示众的材料和看客，病死多少是不必以为不幸的。
chapters.translation: Before that school year was over I was already in Tokyo, because from that time on I felt that medicine was not a thing that mattered. A people that is foolish and weak, however healthy and sturdy their bodies, can only be the stuff and the audience of meaningless public examples; and however many of them die of illness, there is no need to think it a misfortune.
chapters.note: Lu Xun left Sendai for Tokyo in 1906. 凡是 "every, all": 凡是愚弱的国民 "any people that is foolish and weak". 即使…也… "even if …, still …". 如何 "how (much)": 即使体格如何健全 "however healthy the body". 看客 "onlookers".

chapters.text: 所以我们的第一要著，是在改变他们的精神，而善于改变精神的是，我那时以为当然要推文艺，于是想提倡文艺运动了。
chapters.translation: So our first task was to change their spirit, and the thing best at changing the spirit, I thought at the time, was of course literature and art. So I wanted to promote a movement for literature and art.
chapters.note: 要著 "key move", from chess, where 著 is a move: today it is usually printed 要着. CC-CEDICT gives the old form 要著 as the traditional spelling of 要着 "crucial thing", and it is kept as printed. 推 "push forward; name (as the best)": 要推文艺 "one has to name literature".

chapters.text: 在东京的留学生很有学法政理化以至警察工业的，但没有人治文学和美术；可是在冷淡的空气中，也幸而寻到几个同志了，此外又邀集了必须的几个人，商量之后，第一步当然是出杂志，名目是取『新的生命』的意思，因为我们那时大抵带些复古的倾向，所以只谓之新生。
chapters.translation: Among the students in Tokyo there were plenty who studied law and government, physics and chemistry, even police work and industry, but no one who took up literature or art. Still, in that cold air we were lucky enough to find a few comrades, and besides them we gathered the few others we needed. After talking it over, the first step was of course to bring out a magazine. Its name was to mean "new life", and because at the time we mostly leaned toward the old ways, we called it simply 新生, New Life.
chapters.note: 很有…的 "there were very many who …". 治 "work at (a field)". 以至 "and even". 谓之 "call it": the classical pair, 谓 "call" + 之 "it". The leaning to the old ways is in the name: the two-character 新生, in the style of the old books, rather than the plain phrase 新的生命. The 『』 are the book's quotation marks.

chapters.text: 新生的出版之期接近了，但最先就隐去了若干担当文字的人，接着又逃走了资本，结果只剩下不名一钱的三个人。
wfw: take on, be in charge of
chapters.translation: The date for New Life to come out drew near, but first several of the men who were to do the writing slipped away, and then the money ran off too, and in the end there were only three of us left, without a penny between us.
chapters.note: 隐去了若干…的人 "several … men slipped away": the verb comes before its subject, as in 逃走了资本 "the capital ran away". 之 is "of", the classical 的: 出版之期 "the date of publication". 不名一钱 "not own a single coin".

chapters.text: 创始时候既已背时，失败时候当然无可告语，而其后却连这三个人也都为各自的运命所驱策，不能在一处纵谈将来的好梦了，这就是我们的并未产生的新生的结局。
chapters.translation: Since it was out of season when it began, of course there was no one to tell when it failed. And later even we three were driven off, each by his own fate, and could no longer sit in one place and talk freely of our fine dreams for the future. That was the end of our New Life, which was never born.
chapters.note: 为…所… is the formal passive: 为各自的运命所驱策 "were driven by each one's fate". 背时 "out of step with the times". 无可告语 "have no one to tell". 运命 "fate" is today usually 命运.

chapters.text: 我感到未尝经验的无聊，是自此以后的事。
chapters.translation: It was from then on that I felt a dreariness I had never known before.
chapters.note: 无聊 today means "bored, boring"; here it is stronger, an empty pointlessness. 未尝经验的 "never before experienced": 经验 "experience" is used as a verb.

chapters.text: 我当初是不知其所以然的；后来想，凡有一人的主张，得了赞和，是促其前进的，得了反对，是促其奋斗的，独有叫喊的生人中，而生人并无反应，既非赞同，也无反对，如置身毫无边际的荒原，无可措手的了，这是怎样的悲哀呵，我于是以我所感到者为寂寞。
chapters.translation: At first I did not know why. Later I thought: when a man puts forward a view, if it wins approval, that urges him on; if it meets opposition, that urges him to fight. Only when he cries out among strangers, and the strangers make no response at all, neither agreeing nor opposing, is it as if he stood in a boundless wilderness with nothing to set his hand to. What a sorrow that is! And so I gave the name loneliness to what I felt.
chapters.note: 不知其所以然 "did not know the why of it", a classical phrase. 凡有… "whenever there is …". 促其前进 "urges him forward": 其 is "him". 叫喊的生人中 reads as "cry out among strangers"; many later printings have 于 for this 的 (叫喊于生人中), and the text is kept as printed. 以…为… "take … as …": 以我所感到者为寂寞 "took what I felt to be loneliness". 呵 is "ah!". 是…的 wraps a statement: "it is (so) that …".

chapters.text: 这寂寞又一天一天的长大起来，如大毒蛇，缠住了我的灵魂了。
wfw: -ly: often Lu Xun's spelling of 地 before a verb
chapters.translation: And this loneliness grew bigger day by day, and like a great poisonous snake it coiled itself round my soul.
chapters.note: 一天一天的 "day by day": 的 for today's 地. 缠住 "coil tight": 住 after a verb holds it fast.

chapters.text: 然而我虽然自有无端的悲哀，却也并不愤懑，因为这经验使我反省，看见自己了：就是我决不是一个振臂一呼应者云集的英雄。
wfw: raise one's arm and give a cry
chapters.translation: Yet though I had a sorrow of my own that had no cause, I was not angry, for the experience made me look into myself and see myself: I was certainly not a hero who raises his arm, gives one cry, and sees answerers gather like clouds.
chapters.note: 振臂一呼，应者云集 "raise the arm and give one cry, and those who answer gather like clouds": the picture of a born leader. 自有 "have of one's own". 无端 "without cause".

chapters.text: 只是我自己的寂寞是不可不驱除的，因为这于我太痛苦。
chapters.translation: Only, my own loneliness had to be driven out, because to me it was too painful.
chapters.note: 不可不 "may not not": must.

chapters.text: 我于是用了种种法，来麻醉自己的灵魂，使我沈入于国民中，使我回到古代去，后来也亲历或旁观过几样更寂寞、更悲哀的事，都为我所不愿追怀，甘心使他们和我的脑一同消灭在泥土里的，但我的麻醉法却也似乎已经奏了功，再没有青年时候的慷慨激昂的意思了。
chapters.translation: So I used all kinds of means to drug my soul: to sink myself among the people of the nation, to send myself back into antiquity. Later I also lived through, or looked on at, several things lonelier and sadder still. I do not wish to call any of them to mind, and would gladly let them vanish into the earth together with my brain. But my way of drugging myself seems to have worked: I have none of the fiery passion of my youth left.
chapters.note: 沈 is the 1923 spelling of 沉 "sink": 沈入 "sink into". CC-CEDICT lists this 沈 as a variant of 沉; it is kept as printed. 为我所不愿追怀 "are by me not wished to be recalled": the 为…所… passive again. 奏了功 "has had its effect": the word 奏功, split by 了.

chapters.text: Ｓ会馆里有三间屋，相传是往昔曾在院子里的槐树上缢死过一个女人的，现在槐树已经高不可攀了，而这屋还没有人住；许多年，我便寓在这屋里钞古碑。
wfw: it is said, the story goes
chapters.translation: In the S Hostel there were three rooms where, so it was said, a woman had once hanged herself from the locust tree in the courtyard. By now the tree had grown too high to climb, and still no one would live in the rooms. For a good many years I lodged in them, copying old inscriptions.
chapters.note: The S Hostel is the Shaoxing Hostel (绍兴会馆) in Beijing, a guild house for men from Lu Xun's home district; he lived there from 1912 to 1919. 钞 is the 1923 spelling of 抄 "copy" (CC-CEDICT lists it as a variant), kept as printed here and below. 古碑 "old steles": the inscriptions cut on ancient stone tablets. 高不可攀 "too high to climb": no one could hang herself from it now.

chapters.text: 客中少有人来，古碑中也遇不到什么问题和主义，而我的生命却居然暗暗的消去了，这也就是我惟一的愿望。
wfw: -ly: often Lu Xun's spelling of 地 before a verb
chapters.translation: Living away from home, I had few visitors; in the old inscriptions I met with no problems and no -isms; and my life was actually slipping quietly away. That, in fact, was my only wish.
chapters.note: 客中 "while living away from home": the hostel was for men far from home. It is not in CC-CEDICT. 问题和主义 "problems and -isms": the words of a famous quarrel of 1919 among the new writers. 惟一 "only" is today usually printed 唯一; CC-CEDICT has both.

chapters.text: 夏夜，蚊子多了，便摇着蒲扇坐在槐树下，从密叶缝里看那一点一点的青天，晚出的槐蚕又每每冰冷的落在头颈上。
wfw: -ly: often Lu Xun's spelling of 地 before a verb
chapters.translation: On summer nights, when the mosquitoes were many, I would sit under the locust tree waving a palm-leaf fan, and look through the gaps in the thick leaves at the spots of blue sky; and the caterpillars of the locust tree, which come out late, would often drop, ice-cold, on my neck.
chapters.note: 槐蚕 "locust silkworms": the caterpillars that live on the locust tree and let themselves down on threads. It is not in CC-CEDICT. 头颈 "neck" is a dialect word.

chapters.text: 那时偶或来谈的是一个老朋友金心异，将手提的大皮夹放在破桌上，脱下长衫，对面坐下了，因为怕狗，似乎心房还在怦怦的跳动。
wfw: -ly: often Lu Xun's spelling of 地 before a verb
chapters.translation: The one who came now and then to talk was an old friend, Jin Xinyi. He would put the big leather case he carried on the broken table, take off his long gown and sit down facing me. Because he was afraid of dogs, his heart still seemed to be thumping.
chapters.note: 金心异 stands for Qian Xuantong (钱玄同), an editor of the magazine 新青年. The name comes from a story by the conservative writer Lin Shu, who used it to mock him; Lu Xun borrows it as a joke. 偶或 "now and then" is not in CC-CEDICT.

chapters.text: 『你钞了这些有什么用？』
chapters.translation: 'What is the use of copying these?'
chapters.note: 你钞了这些有什么用 "you copy these: what use is there?". 用 here is a noun, "use".

chapters.text: 有一夜，他翻着我那古碑的钞本，发了研究的质问了。
chapters.translation: One night, leafing through my copies of the inscriptions, he put the question like a scholar making an inquiry.
chapters.note: The question comes before the sentence that introduces it. 钞本 "hand copy" is today 抄本; it is not in CC-CEDICT. 发了研究的质问 "sent out a researching question".

chapters.text: 『没有什么用。』
chapters.translation: 'No use at all.'

chapters.text: 『那么，你钞他是什么意思呢？』
chapters.translation: 'Then what is the point of copying them?'
chapters.note: 他 here is "them": the inscriptions. In the 1920s 他 could stand for things as well as people.

chapters.text: 『没有什么意思。』
chapters.translation: 'No point at all.'

chapters.text: 『我想，你可以做点文章……』
chapters.translation: 'I think you could write something…'
chapters.note: 做文章 "make writing": write an essay or a piece. 点 "a bit".

chapters.text: 我懂得他的意思了，他们正办新青年，然而那时仿佛不特没有人来赞同，并且也还没有人来反对，我想，他们许是感到寂寞了，但是说：
chapters.translation: I understood what he meant. They were running New Youth, but at the time it seemed that not only had no one come to agree with them, no one had come to oppose them either. I thought they were perhaps feeling lonely. But I said:
chapters.note: 新青年 New Youth was the magazine of the new literature, founded in 1915 and edited in Beijing from 1917. 不特…并且… "not only … but also": 不特 is the bookish 不但. 许 "perhaps" is the bookish 也许.

chapters.text: 『假如一间铁屋子，是绝无窗户而万难破毁的，里面有许多熟睡的人们，不久都要闷死了，然而是从昏睡入死灭，并不感到就死的悲哀。
chapters.translation: 'Suppose there is an iron house with no windows at all, and all but impossible to break. Inside are many people fast asleep, who will soon all suffocate. But they will pass from sleep into death, and will not feel the sorrow of dying.
chapters.note: 绝无 "utterly without". 万难 "ten thousand difficulties": nearly impossible. 闷死 "die shut in", suffocate. 就死 "go to one's death": 就 is "go toward". This iron house is the most quoted picture in the book.

chapters.text: 现在你大嚷起来，惊起了较为清醒的几个人，使这不幸的少数者来受无可挽救的临终的苦楚，你倒以为对得起他们么？』
chapters.translation: Now if you raise a great shout and wake the few who sleep lightest, and make this unlucky few suffer the agony of dying with no hope of rescue, do you really think you are doing right by them?'
chapters.note: 大嚷起来 "start to shout loud". 对得起 "do right by (someone)". 倒 "on the contrary": 你倒以为… "and you think …, do you?".

chapters.text: 『然而几个人既然起来，你不能说决没有毁坏这铁屋的希望。』
chapters.translation: 'But since a few have got up, you cannot say there is no hope of breaking the iron house.'
chapters.note: 决没有 "surely there is no": 决 stresses the negative.

chapters.text: 是的，我虽然自有我的确信，然而说到希望，却是不能抹杀的，因为希望是在于将来，决不能以我之必无的证明，来折服了他之所谓可有，于是我终于答应他也做文章了，这便是最初的一篇狂人日记。
chapters.translation: Yes: I had my own conviction, but when it came to hope, that could not be wiped out, because hope lies in the future, and I could never use my proof that there was none to defeat his claim that there might be. So in the end I agreed that I too would write. That was the first piece, A Madman's Diary.
chapters.note: 以我之必无的证明，来折服了他之所谓可有 "with my proof that (it) surely is not, to win over his claim that (it) may be": 之 is the classical 的, twice. 狂人日记 A Madman's Diary, the first story of the book, came out in 新青年 in May 1918.

chapters.text: 从此以后，便一发而不可收，每写些小说模样的文章，以敷衍朋友们的嘱托，积久就有了十馀篇。
wfw: once started, could not be stopped
oblige, do just to get done
chapters.translation: From then on, once started, I could not stop. Each time I would write something in the shape of a story, to oblige my friends after a fashion, and as they piled up there came to be more than ten.
chapters.note: 一发而不可收 "once shot, it cannot be called back". 敷衍 "do something just to get it done": he speaks of the stories as made to satisfy his friends. 馀 is the 1923 spelling of 余 "and more": 十馀篇 "ten-odd pieces". It is kept as printed.

chapters.text: 在我自己，本以为现在是已经并非一个切迫而不能已于言的人了，但或者也还未能忘怀于当日自己的寂寞的悲哀罢，所以有时候仍不免呐喊几声，聊以慰藉那在寂寞里奔驰的猛士，使他不惮于前驱。
wfw: just to, in some small way
chapters.translation: For myself, I had thought I was no longer a man so pressed that he cannot keep from speaking out. But perhaps I have still not been able to forget the sorrow of my own loneliness in those days, and so I still sometimes cannot help giving a few shouts, to give some small comfort to the brave men galloping on through the loneliness, so that they do not fear to ride in front.
chapters.note: 不能已于言 "cannot stop from speech": a classical phrase, in which 已 is "stop". 聊以 "just to, in some small way". 不惮 "not fear" is bookish. 前驱 "ride ahead": the vanguard. 罢 is the old spelling of 吧, here "perhaps it is …".

chapters.text: 至于我的喊声是勇猛或是悲哀，是可憎或是可笑，那倒是不暇顾及的；但既然是呐喊，则当然须听将令的了，所以我往往不恤用了曲笔，在药的瑜儿的坟上平空添上一个花环，在明天里也不叙单四嫂子竟没有做到看见儿子的梦，因为那时的主将是不主张消极的，至于自己，却也并不愿将自以为苦的寂寞，再来传染给也如我那年青时候似的正做着好梦的青年。
wfw: bent brush (writing that bends the truth)
Mrs Shan the Fourth (in 明天)
like, as if (after what it compares)
chapters.translation: As to whether my shouts are brave or sad, hateful or laughable, I have no time to think about that. But since they are a call to arms, I must of course obey the general's orders. So I have often not scrupled to bend my brush: in 药 Medicine I put a wreath, out of nowhere, on the grave of Yu'er, and in 明天 Tomorrow I do not tell that Mrs Shan the Fourth never did get to dream of seeing her son, because the commanders of the time were against gloom. As for me, I have no wish either to pass on the loneliness I found so bitter to the young, who are dreaming fine dreams as I did when I was young.
chapters.note: 药 and 明天 are two of the stories in this book. 曲笔 "bent brush": writing that turns from the plain truth. 将令 "the general's orders" and 主将 "the commanders" are the editors of 新青年. 不恤 "not care about" is bookish. 平空 "out of thin air" is today usually 凭空; CC-CEDICT has both. 单四嫂子 "Fourth Sister-in-law Shan" is the widow of 明天, who loses her small son.

chapters.text: 这样说来，我的小说和艺术的距离之远，也就可想而知了，然而到今日还能蒙着小说的名，甚而至于且有成集的机会，无论如何总不能不说是一件徼幸的事，但徼幸虽使我不安于心，而悬揣人间暂时还有读者，则究竟也仍然是高兴的。
wfw: no matter what, in any case
chapters.translation: Seen this way, how far my stories are from art can easily be imagined. Yet that to this day they can still go by the name of stories, and even have the chance to become a book, must in any case be called a stroke of luck. And though the luck makes me uneasy at heart, still, to guess that there are readers in the world for the time being is, after all, a pleasure.
chapters.note: 这样说来 "speaking in this way": "so". 距离之远 "the farness of the distance": 之 for 的 again. 蒙着小说的名 "bearing the name of fiction": 蒙 is "be covered with, receive". 徼幸 is the 1923 spelling of 侥幸 "a stroke of luck" (CC-CEDICT lists it as a variant), kept as printed. 悬揣 "guess in the air" is bookish.

chapters.text: 所以我竟将我的短篇小说结集起来，而且付印了，又因为上面所说的缘由，便称之为呐喊。
chapters.translation: So I have after all gathered my short stories together and sent them to the printer, and for the reasons given above I have called them 呐喊, Call to Arms.
chapters.note: 称之为 "call it (as)": 之 "it", 为 "as". The title takes up the 呐喊几声 "a few shouts" of 22.1.

chapters.text: 一九二二年十二月三日，鲁迅记于北京。
chapters.translation: Written by Lu Xun in Beijing, 3 December 1922.
chapters.note: 一九二二 is a year written figure by figure: 1922. 记 "note down" closes a preface. 鲁迅 is the pen name of Zhou Shuren (周树人).
